text:
alex: Heads up — hitting weird behavior in the Go SDK generator streaming when using chunked outputs + context cancel. After cancel, Recv() sometimes blocks and we keep getting chunks for ~100-300ms. Anyone seen this?

tanvi: Hmm, that sounds like the HTTP request context might not be wired into the underlying read. Can you paste a minimal repro?

alex: Sure, simplified repro:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.GeneratorStream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for {
  tok, err := resp.Recv()
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { log.Println("stream err:", err); break }
  fmt.Println(tok.Text)
}
```
Canceling the ctx or hitting the timeout reliably returns quickly in non-streaming calls, but here Recv() often blocks ~200ms before returning context.Canceled.

matt: Are you on token auth with refresh enabled? I vaguely remember a race where midstream auth refresh caused the server to finish the current chunk batch before honoring cancel. Any logs?

alex: Logs:```
2024-11-12T15:21:02.120Z INFO stream: recv frame len=8192
2024-11-12T15:21:02.321Z WARN client: context canceled requestID=abc123
2024-11-12T15:21:02.521Z INFO stream: recv frame len=4096
```
You can see the cancel at 15:21:02.321 but we still get another frame at .521.

jen: I think we've got two orthogonal issues: (1) client->http transport needs WithContext wired so that Cancel propagates to the request body reader; (2) the server/runtime may buffer chunk batches and finish sending an already-started write operation even after cancellation. Workarounds: open request with http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, ...), or wrap ReadCloser with a ctx-aware reader that returns on ctx.Done().

tanvi: Example workaround for the client side:```go
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, body)
resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
// then stream from resp.Body
```
Also we should add a note in the Go SDK doc: "GeneratorStream should be created with a context; cancellation should cancel the underlying http request" so parity with other SDKs is explicit.

matt: Agreed — we should have an e2e test asserting that cancel -> Recv returns context.Canceled within X ms (and not hang for seconds). I'll draft a test in go-sdk/integration that uses a fake runtime that simulates mid-chunk writes.

alex: I'll open an issue with a minimal repro and attach the logs. Can someone from runtime confirm whether they intentionally drain an in-flight write or if that can be made interruptible? @matt @tanvi :raised_hands:

devex-bot: Created issue #4821: "go-sdk: streaming Recv does not return promptly on context cancel with chunked responses" (assigned to devex).

jen: Filing checklist suggestion: repro code, exact SDK version, transport (net/http), http2 vs http1, whether auth refresh was active, and a small flow diagram of the expected behavior vs observed.

alex: Thanks — will add those. Quick note: this felt different from the "handshake cancellation" bugs in the past; calling it out separately because the symptom is "late in-flight chunk arrival" rather than goroutine leak.

matt: Also adding to the onboarding docs: sampleapp should show the recommended pattern: create ctx at callsite, pass it through, and always call cancel() / drain response on error.

alex: Perfect — thanks all.
